questions.text: What is the power of a convex lens having a focal length of 50 cm?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the formula P(D) = 100 / f(cm) for quick calculation without converting to meters. 100 / 50 = 2 D. Worked Solution: Power (P) = 1 / f(m). Focal length f = 50 cm = 0.5 m. P = 1 / 0.5 = 2 Dioptres. Since the lens is convex, power is positive.

questions.text: Select the number that will come next in the following series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check differences between terms: 4, 6, 8, 10. Differences increase by 2 each time. Next difference = 12. 30 + 12 = 42. Full Method: The series follows the pattern n × (n+1): 1×2=2, 2×3=6, 3×4=12, 4×5=20, 5×6=30. The 6th term is 6×7 = 42. Alternatively, successive differences are consecutive even numbers (4, 6, 8, 10), so next difference is 12, giving 30+12=42.

questions.text: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 20%, what is the percentage increase in its volume?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Volume ∝ r³. New radius factor = 1.2. Volume factor = (1.2)³ = 1.728. % Increase = (1.728 - 1) × 100 = 72.8%. Worked: Original Volume V₁ = (4/3)πr³. New radius = 1.2r. New Volume V₂ = (4/3)π(1.2r)³ = 1.728 × (4/3)πr³ = 1.728 V₁. Increase = 0.728 V₁ = 72.8%.

questions.text: Find the missing term in the following alphabet series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Write alphabet positions (A=1, B=2... using EJOTY for 5,10,15,20,25). Differences between terms: +2, +3, +4, +5. Next difference is +6. O(15) + 6 = 21 (U). Worked Solution: A(1) -> C(3) diff 2; C(3) -> F(6) diff 3; F(6) -> J(10) diff 4; J(10) -> O(15) diff 5. Pattern increases by 1 each step. Next diff = 6. 15 + 6 = 21 -> U.

questions.text: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground is 30°. On walking 20 metres towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 60°. What is the height of the tower (in metres)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Formula for height when angles are 30° and 60°: h = d / (cot 30° - cot 60°) = 20 / (√3 - 1/√3) = 20 / (2/√3) = 10√3 m. Full Method: Let height = h. In Δ with 60°, base = h/√3. In Δ with 30°, base = h√3. Difference in bases = h√3 - h/√3 = 20. => h(3-1)/√3 = 20 => 2h/√3 = 20 => h = 10√3 m.

questions.text: The filtration of blood in the human nephron takes place specifically in which capillary network under high pressure?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Remember the functional sequence: Filtration → Glomerulus (high pressure capillary bed); Selective Reabsorption → PCT; Concentration of Urine → Loop of Henle. Filtration occurs only in the Glomerulus. Full Solution: The glomerulus is a tuft of capillaries formed by the afferent arteriole (wider) and efferent arteriole (narrower). This difference in diameter creates high hydrostatic pressure inside the glomerular capillaries, forcing water and solutes out of the blood into the Bowman's capsule (ultrafiltration). The PCT and Loop of Henle are tubular structures involved in reabsorption, not the primary site of filtration.

questions.text: What is the primary function of red blood cells in the human body?
questions.solution: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, a protein that binds to oxygen in the lungs and transports it to tissues throughout the body. Fighting infections is the role of white blood cells, clotting is performed by platelets, and hormone production is primarily a function of endocrine glands.

questions.text: As per the original text of the Constitution of India adopted on 26th November 1949, how many Schedules did it contain?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Remember the baseline 'Original 8, Current 12'. The 9th Schedule was added in 1951 (1st Amendment), 10th in 1985 (52nd Amendment), 11th & 12th in 1992 (73rd & 74th Amendments). Option A (Eight) is the only figure matching the 1949 status. Worked Solution: The Constitution of India, when adopted on 26 November 1949, had 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. The 9th Schedule was inserted by the 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951. The 10th Schedule (Anti-Defection) was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985. The 11th Schedule (Panchayats) and 12th Schedule (Municipalities) were added by the 73rd and 74th Amendment Acts, 1992 respectively, bringing the current total to 12.

questions.text: Which is the largest state in India by geographical area?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate population leaders (UP, Maharashtra) — area leaders are usually central/western large states (Rajasthan, MP). Rajasthan (~3.42 lakh sq km) > MP (~3.08 lakh sq km). Step-by-step: As per Census 2011, Rajasthan covers 342,239 sq km, making it the largest. Madhya Pradesh is second. Maharashtra is third. Uttar Pradesh is fourth in area but first in population.

questions.text: The 'Instrument of Accession' signed by Maharaja Hari Singh in October 1947 legally acceded which princely state to the Dominion of India?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): Hyderabad (Option A) was integrated via Operation Polo in 1948. Junagadh (Option B) acceded to Pakistan initially, then India after a plebiscite. Travancore (Option D) initially declared independence but joined India before 1947 end. Only Jammu & Kashmir (Option C) executed the Instrument of Accession on 26 Oct 1947 under specific circumstances. Step-by-step: The Instrument of Accession was a legal document executed by Maharaja Hari Singh on 26 October 1947. By executing this document under the provisions of the Indian Independence Act 1947, the Maharaja agreed to accede the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir to the Dominion of India. Lord Mountbatten accepted it on 27 October 1947.
questions.topic: Modern Indian History (Integration of Princely States)

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GIVE' is written as '79225' and 'BOAT' is written as '215120'. How will 'MOON' be written in that language?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the EJOTY concept (E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Y=25) to instantly recall alphabet positions. The code is the concatenation of positional values. M=13, O=15, O=15, N=14 → 13151514. Full Solution: Decode the logic from examples. G(7) I(9) V(22) E(5) → 79225. B(2) O(15) A(1) T(20) → 215120. Each letter is replaced by its position in the English alphabet. Applying same to MOON: M(13), O(15), O(15), N(14) = 13151514.

questions.text: A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. B and C together can complete it in 15 days. C and A together can complete it in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
questions.solution: Shortcut: LCM Method. Total Work = LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60 units. Efficiency (A+B) = 5 units/day, (B+C) = 4 units/day, (C+A) = 3 units/day. Adding: 2(A+B+C) = 12 units/day => (A+B+C) = 6 units/day. Efficiency of A = 6 - 4 = 2 units/day. Time for A = 60/2 = 30 days. Full Method: 1/A + 1/B = 1/12, 1/B + 1/C = 1/15, 1/C + 1/A = 1/20. Adding gives 2(1/A+1/B+1/C) = 1/5 => 1/A+1/B+1/C = 1/10. Subtracting 1/B+1/C=1/15 gives 1/A = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30. Time = 30 days.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers does NOT originate from the Amarkantak plateau?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): Amarkantak (Maikal Hills) is a major watershed. Narmada (A) flows West; Son (B) flows North; Mahanadi (C) flows East. All three originate here. Tapti (D) originates from Multai in Betul district (Satpura range), South of Amarkantak. Eliminate A, B, C as they share the source. Step-by-step: The Amarkantak plateau in Anuppur district, Madhya Pradesh, is the source of three major rivers: Narmada (westward), Son (northward, tributary of Ganga), and Mahanadi (eastward). The Tapti river originates from the Satpura range near Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh, which is geographically distinct from the Amarkantak plateau.

questions.text: Which of the following mountain peaks is the highest peak located entirely within Indian territory?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate border peaks first. K2 lies in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK). Kanchenjunga is shared with Nepal. Nanda Devi (7,816 m) lies entirely in Uttarakhand, India. Kamet (7,756 m) is also in India but lower than Nanda Devi. Worked Solution: K2 (8,611 m) is the world's second-highest peak but is located in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of POK. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the third-highest globally but straddles the India-Nepal border. Nanda Devi (7,816 m) is the highest peak situated completely within India. Kamet is the second-highest peak entirely in India but is lower than Nanda Devi.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the expression \((12^{41} + 13^{31} + 17^{21} + 18^{11})\)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of 4 for unit digits 2,3,7,8. Powers 41,31,21,11 give remainders 1,3,1,3 yielding unit digits 2,7,7,2; sum=18→8. Full: \(12^{41}\to2^{41}\to2^1=2\); \(13^{31}\to3^{31}\to3^3=7\); \(17^{21}\to7^{21}\to7^1=7\); \(18^{11}\to8^{11}\to8^3=2\); total unit digit \(=(2+7+7+2)=18\to8\).
